searchText: I have a question about status codes, does the beacon chain does anything with them? you mean error codes in Engine API? no i mean, "INVALID" "VALID" and "SYNCING" Ah, these ones. `INVALID` invalidates the beacon block, `VALID` is valid and means that the block is accepted if the beacon chain state transition says so as well, `SYNCING` turns beacon node into syncing mode, this mode has a lot of implications, validator can't attest and propose while syncing, all beacon blocks are optimistically processed while EL is syncing and aren't surfaced to both, user and other beacon nodes, until they are fully validated -- when the first `VALID` response is returned. `INVALID` may also invalidate a segment of a chain if `latestValidHash` points to ancestor that is far from the head of this chain okay thank you are there updated graphics for https://hackmd.io/@n0ble/consensus_api_design_space#Block-processing-flow for Kintsugi someone's already made? Nothing that I am aware of okay, thanks do you want to make some? Hey guys, has any decision been made with respect to the ETH1_FOLLOW_DISTANCE ? I would assume a 2048 block period would no longer be needed before recognising validator deposits as final and that instead we could lean on finalised head for when a deposit is recognised and pushed to the activation queue? Is that accurate? Is such a change out of scope for a minimal viable merge? It's out of scope for the minimal merge and considered for a clean up fork. The end design is not yet settled down and using finality is one of the potential ways. Ideally, the proposer of the next block includes deposits made in the previous block with proofs linked to `ExecutionPayload.state_root` or even beacon block/state root but it would require beacon chain to verify hexary trie proofs which isn't desired dependency. I've filed an issue with one pretty painful edge case, https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/issues/2732 Thanks to <@!792822129019584562> for raising this in the <#892088344438255616> Personally I prefer having an explicit `engine_getBlock` RPC (plus any other required RPCs) than exposing all of `eth_` on the EL<=>CL channel, I feel like exposing the entire `eth` namespace adds a lot of surface area to the interface. At a minimum I think the spec should enumerate which `eth` methods are needed by the CL. Apologies if this is the wrong place to ask. Is there any where I can learn more regarding validators sharing an eth1 endpoint post merge?

excerpts.author: funnygiulio
excerpts.content: I have a question about status codes, does the beacon chain does anything with them?

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: you mean error codes in Engine API?

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: Ah, these ones. `INVALID` invalidates the beacon block, `VALID` is valid and means that the block is accepted if the beacon chain state transition says so as well, `SYNCING` turns beacon node into syncing mode, this mode has a lot of implications, validator can't attest and propose while syncing, all beacon blocks are optimistically processed while EL is syncing and aren't surfaced to both, user and other beacon nodes, until they are fully validated -- when the first `VALID` response is returned. `INVALID` may also invalidate a segment of a chain if `latestValidHash`  points to ancestor that is far from the head of this chain

excerpts.author: okyne
excerpts.content: Hey guys, has any decision been made with respect to the ETH1_FOLLOW_DISTANCE ? I would assume a 2048 block period would no longer be needed before recognising validator deposits as final and that instead we could lean on finalised head for when a deposit is recognised and pushed to the activation queue? Is that accurate? Is such a change out of scope for a minimal viable merge?

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: It's out of scope for the minimal merge and considered for a clean up fork. The end design is not yet settled down and using finality is one of the potential ways. Ideally, the proposer of the next block includes deposits made in the previous block with proofs linked to `ExecutionPayload.state_root` or even beacon block/state root but it would require beacon chain to verify hexary trie proofs which isn't desired dependency.

Thanks to <@!792822129019584562> for raising this in the <#892088344438255616>

excerpts.author: ryanleeschneider
excerpts.content: Personally I prefer having an explicit `engine_getBlock` RPC (plus any other required RPCs) than exposing all of `eth_` on the EL<=>CL channel, I feel like exposing the entire `eth` namespace adds a lot of surface area to the interface.  At a minimum I think the spec should enumerate which `eth` methods are needed by the CL.
